business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Procurement of Culinary and Ceremonial Grade Matcha

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate tax distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic codification heritage; commercial companies governed by the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (in force 1 February 2019; tariff and market-access framework for matcha sourced from Japan)
Luxembourg–Japan Income and Capital Tax Treaty (1992; elimination of double taxation on procurement margins, royalties and export distributions)
Luxembourg–Hong Kong SAR Double Taxation Agreement (2007; withholding tax relief applicable to Hong Kong corporate partners holding SCSp interests)
Luxembourg–People's Republic of China DTA (1994; source taxation relief for PRC-linked raw material supply chains)
People's Republic of China–Luxembourg Bilateral Investment Treaty (1987; investment protection applicable to PRC mid-stream investors)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML/CFT Law), as amended notably by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE/LBR), as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (SCSp regime amended by Law of 23 July 2016); CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 January 2017 on the RCS. RBE access is tiered: full access for competent authorities and obliged entities; public access only upon demonstration of legitimate interest (CJEU C-37/20 and C-601/20, WM and Sovim).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation / business registration of each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or domestic notary (e.g., Hong Kong Companies Registry for HK partners; ACRA for SOP/LLP partners)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the competent authority of the registering jurisdiction; if the jurisdiction is not an Apostille Contracting State, full consular legalization chain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport pages of all partners, ultimate beneficial owners and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport issuing authority or public notary of the nationality jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the notarized certification, followed by sworn translation into French or German where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country commercial registry (issuance date within 30 days before submission)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified Luxembourg translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to Luxembourg incorporation counsel and registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or equivalent authority of the place of signature; affixed with corporate seal where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / consular legalization of the notarial act, plus sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth attestation letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner, co-signed by the Luxembourg registered agent and AML compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of each UBO outside Luxembourg where required; apostille/legalization per signature-jurisdiction; no apostille required for signatures given before the Luxembourg registered agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-closing screening against: (i) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated Lists; (iii) OFAC SDN/Non-SDN lists (standard for USD SWIFT TT correspondent clearing); (iv) Luxembourg Ministry of Finance national freezes and restrictive measures; and (v) CSSF-published regulatory warnings. Mandatory negative-news/PEP-locator checks (World-Check or equivalent) on all partners, UBOs at or above 25%, and authorized signatories; enhanced due diligence for PEPs and for counterparties resident in or transiting sanctioned jurisdictions; documentation of the AML risk file and retention for five (5) years after termination of the business relationship per Article 9-1 of the AML/CFT Law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) at www.lbr.lu — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated on behalf of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp name must be composed in Latin script; if a non-Latin script is used, a Latin-script transliteration must be filed for RCS insertion. The constitutive document must be drawn in French, German or Luxembourgish; a document in any other language requires a sworn translation. The name must begin or end with the token 'SCSp' (or the full 'Société en Commandite Spéciale') to evidence the limited liability of the special partners. The name must be distinguishable and not misleading as to activity (Law of 10 August 1915, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 January 2017).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: OPC / SICAV / SICAF / SICAR / fonds de placement
Luxembourg / État / national (misleading state or public-sector connotation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If LBR/RCS rejects the name, the registrar issues a reasoned refusal through the LBR portal. Remedy options: (1) file a fresh name clearance request citing a materially distinct name (no cooling-off period); and/or (2) contest the refusal by unilateral application (requête unilatérale) to the Commercial Chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within one (1) month of the reasoned refusal, through a Luxembourg avocat, requesting an order compelling registration; urgent relief may be sought by référé where delay causes irreparable loss. An approved reservation is automatically renewable at expiry for one further six-month window; no statutory premium is payable for extension.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The SCSp must maintain a genuine registered office ('siège') in Luxembourg, being a physical address where statutory records, correspondence and accounts are kept. Use of a licensed professional domiciliation agent (prestataire de services de domiciliation) is standard market practice and satisfies the statutory mandate, provided the agent is fully licensed; a pure 'virtual' office without a Luxembourg-licensed agent and without a local bank account and local bookkeeping is unlawful for an SCSp structured as a pass-through wholesale trade vehicle.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated annual probability ≤5%): unannounced inspections are infrequent for a Low_Risk_Standard wholesale distribution SCSp with current RBE filings, a licensed domiciliation agent and an active Luxembourg bank account. The inspection probability increases to a moderate band (20–35%) only upon AML trigger events (OFAC hit, RBE default, cash-intensive payments, or inconsistencies in UBO declarations).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service — year-one (pro-rata pre-incorporation commitment)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate services provider (authorized AML compliance resource)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark package fee inclusive of World-Check or equivalent screening reports

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published tariff for commercial account opening and sanctions-screen integration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee; Administration de l'enregistrement VAT registration itself is free of charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: 10% contingency on notarization/apostille and translation lines

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Act of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 61 to 74 (Société en Commandite Spéciale); Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the SCSp; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 30 July 2013 on RCS electronic filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: RCS registration application (demande d'inscription au RCS) filed electronically with the signed partnership agreement (contrat de société)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: Luxembourg law imposes no minimum capital, no paid-up capital, and no escrow requirement for an SCSp; partners freely determine the amount and form of contributions in the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The general manager and the partners hereby adopt, in lieu of a board, this First Resolution of the SCSp: (1) The partnership agreement, contribution schedules and subscription statements are approved in final form. (2) All limited partner subscriptions are accepted in the amounts recorded in the contribution ledger, fully subscribed and not withdrawn. (3) The registered office stated in the partnership agreement is adopted as the SCSp's sole seat and address of service in Luxembourg. (4) [Name of manager] is appointed Gérant with authority to represent the SCSp, open bank accounts, obtain licences, sign trade contracts, file declarations and complete all formalities. (5) This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private drafting; no pre-registration government approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership agreement (contrat de société) in Luxembourg legal form, specifying the SCSp name, registered office, corporate objects limited to wholesale trade in organic matcha powder, subscription amounts, profit-sharing and management. Have the general partner and all limited partners execute the agreement; remote electronic signatures may be used if valid under Luxembourg e-commerce law. If a partner contributes assets in kind, arrange a contribution statement reflecting fair value and ownership transfer.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the general partner and limited partners
Power of attorney if signing through an agent
Valuation or contribution statement for in-kind contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agreement is queried by counsel or the registry, amend it by private deed and re-execute the corrected version before filing; obtain a certified translation where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of the Luxembourg Registered Office and Domiciliation Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved domiciliation agent or commercial landlord in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a registered office in Luxembourg City or another approved address through a licensed domiciliation agent or a commercial lease. Execute a domiciliation agreement and obtain the landlord's written consent to register the SCSp at that address. The registered office must not be a post-office box and must accept legal process for the entity.
required_dossiers: Passport or corporate extract of the service provider
Power of attorney to the domiciliation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the address is rejected at filing, obtain an alternative approved domiciliation agreement and update the partnership agreement and RCS application before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration Filing and Official Publication of the SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the LBR electronic portal, complete the RCS application form for a special limited partnership, upload the signed partnership agreement and annexes, pay the applicable state fee and submit for legal review. Upon approval, LBR issues the RCS excerpt and publishes the registration in the official electronic compilation of companies and associations (RESA). Retain the RCS extract as conclusive evidence of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries a clause, submit a corrective deed through the same LBR workspace and explain the legal basis. If the proposed name is refused, reserve a new available name and refile the amended registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Beneficial Ownership and Regulatory Approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED); Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA); Ministry of the Economy
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the RCS extract, obtain the Luxembourg tax registration number, register for VAT if the SCSp will make taxable transactions in Luxembourg, and file beneficial owner information in the RBE. If the SCSp will import or distribute organic matcha powder as a food business operator, complete ALVA food business operator registration, apply for the trade/import organic certificate under EU Regulation 2018/848, and, if applicable, obtain the establishment authorisation required under Luxembourg commercial establishment law.
required_dossiers: Beneficial owner declaration and identity documents
ALVA food business operator registration form
Organic certification or organic import certificate application under EU Regulation 2018/848
Establishment authorisation dossier if physical premises are used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ALVA or the Ministry requests corrective information, submit the supplementary documents through the official e-file and, if necessary, obtain a temporary approval while the dossier is completed. Late VAT registration can be regularised by voluntary filing with AED; RBE omissions are curable by immediate online amendment without penalty if made after registry reminder.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry and Commerce (Ministère de l'Économie); food safety and organic control: Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA); environmental authority: Administration de l'environnement.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (commercial/industrial establishment authorisation) under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to regulated professions; combined with ALVA food business operator registration and, for organic product, an EU organic trade/import certificate. No separate manufacturing permit is required for wholesale distribution of organic matcha powder.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA report for pure wholesale distribution; Category C registration/declaration applies only where the SCSp operates storage or repacking premises above minor threshold capacity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No significant point-source industrial discharges arise from matcha powder trade. If storage or repacking is performed, comply with applicable municipal wastewater discharge standards under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 3 June 2009, maintain dust/PM10 below occupational exposure limits, segregate organic product to avoid contamination, and manage packaging waste under Luxembourg waste law of 18 July 2010.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval by the municipal fire-prevention authority or the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) for premises storing combustible dust or palletised goods; structural load inspection for shelving and storage areas; occupational health and safety verification by the Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines – ITM), including sanitary facilities, emergency exits and workplace accessibility.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / GST / Sales and Use Tax

mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the monetary authority; in parallel the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institutions and payment services. No dedicated foreign exchange control administration exists, as Luxembourg forms part of the eurozone; the regulatory regime derives from the EU Treaty, the Economic and Monetary Union framework, and the anti-money laundering directives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full convertibility for current and capital transactions, underpinned by Articles 63 to 65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no domestic foreign exchange permits, no restriction on profit remittance, and no approval applicable to foreign investors wiring funds to a Luxembourg SCSp. The only material prerequisites are compliance with commercial bank KYC, the CSSF AML/CFT rulebook, EU sanctions screening, and the balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligation executed through the resident credit institution. Withholding tax may apply on certain distributions under Luxembourg domestic law, but convertibility itself and the ability to remit profits overseas are unhindered.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No Luxembourg statutory rule mandates the surrender of export proceeds to the Central Bank or the government. There is no minimum conversion ratio for EUR retained earnings, no requirement to repatriate proceeds within a prescribed number of days, and no prohibition on maintaining foreign currency accounts. Export invoices for organic matcha powder are paid directly into a designated Luxembourg operating account, and the only legal requirement is for the resident credit institution to capture the cross-border payment data for BCL balance-of-payments statistics, usually on a monthly or quarterly reporting cycle.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM. An EU-authorised or passportable e-money institution can legally provide the SCSp with a virtual IBAN and execute SEPA and cross-border payments, but availability depends on the EMI's own risk appetite for partnership vehicles. Non-EU offshore digital EMIs are generally not permissible as the sole cash-flow clearing channel for an SCSp with genuine trade substance, due to CSSF AML outsourcing expectations, restrictions on the type of payable account, and the risk of unlicensed payment activity. Recommendation: use a regulated EU EMI for low-value disbursements or optional API-driven treasury sweeps, but maintain a commercial bank account as the primary settlement rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under CSSF AML/CFT guidance, remote onboarding is legally possible where the bank applies approved digital identification and eIDAS-compliant electronic signatures. In practice, however, most Luxembourg banks require at least a virtual or physical interview with the managing general partner, a director of the SCSp, or the authorised signatory. For non-EU ultimate beneficial owners or structures where the general partner is itself a corporate vehicle, banks commonly require an initial in-person meeting or a notarised confirmation of identity signed before a Luxembourg notary. The practical standard is therefore that physical presence is not universally mandatory, but the bank has full discretion to require attendance if any enhanced due diligence trigger is present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SCSp appears as a low-substance pass-through vehicle with zero employees and a corporate general partner domiciled in an offshore trust jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the signed SCSp partnership agreement, extract from the Luxembourg trade and companies register, a substance memorandum for the tax year, actual lease agreement for Luxembourg premises, evidence that management decisions are taken by individuals in Luxembourg, and notarised corporate documentation proving the general partner has substance in its own jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth or source of funds inconsistency caused by capital contributions sourced from multiple non-resident investors or layered Asian trust structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver audited or certified bank statements for each investor, signed subscription letters, a full capital introduction trail from the depositing account to the SCSp bank account, tax references or tax residency certificates, and a capital account statement prepared by the Luxembourg partnership administrator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Matcha trade involving high-risk counterparty jurisdictions or frequent third-party settlement requests where payments are not routed directly to the producer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare the complete trade file: ISIC 4631 procurement contract, organic matcha certification under JAS or EU Organic Regulation, warehouse receipts, certificates of origin, shipping and packing lists, customs declarations, supplier corporate registration documents, and a written commercial rationale for each prepayment, split settlement, or commission payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The ultimate beneficial owner cannot be identified due to layered ownership through nominee shareholders, silent partnerships, or missing updated UBO declarations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File a 25% plus transparency chart, signed declaration of trust or nominee waiver, notarised passport copies of each individual in the ownership chain, and a confirmation application to register the ultimate individual in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), so that the UBO is demonstrably traceable and current.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions should be routed exclusively through a commercial bank wire to the SCSp's dedicated corporate account using SWIFT MT103; for euro payments, SEPA or TARGET2 credit transfer is also permissible. To satisfy both banking compliance and statistical reporting, the remittance instruction must state the correct balance-of-payments purpose code. For direct participation in a Luxembourg SCSp, the sending bank should map the payment to the inward direct investment category, commonly reported as code S250 for other direct investment capital in an EU/EEA entity; if the capital is structured as a shareholder loan, code S210 for loans and deposits should be used instead. The receiving bank will perform beneficiary verification against the corporate board resolution, the passport excerpt of the authorised signatory, and the partnership agreement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for organic matcha powder procurement can be cleared via SWIFT MT103 for standard telegraphic transfer, via a commercial letter of credit issued under ICC Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600) for higher-value or first-time supplier shipments, and via SEPA Instant Credit for EU-based distributors. For non-EU suppliers, correspondent clearing is arranged through the banking partner's global network. When a letter of credit is selected, the issuing bank must receive exact presentation terms: commercial invoice, full set of clean on board bills of lading or airway bills, packing list, certificate of origin, phytosanitary certificate, and the relevant matcha grade certificate under the applicable organic standard. All documentation must be consistent with the HS sub-headings 090210 or 090220 and with the ISIC 4631 trading model.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward contract, deliverable, on EUR/USD, EUR/JPY or USD/JPY with matched maturity to a defined matcha trade invoice
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on currencies subject to limited deliverability, used strictly to hedge trade exposure arising from procurement in restricted jurisdictions
Cross-currency swap between EUR/USD or EUR/JPY to manage long-term capital and operating cash-flow risk
European-style purchased FX option for contingent protection against adverse exchange-rate movement without speculative positioning

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year, during the anniversary month of the initial RBE registration; updated declaration due within one month of any partnership-interest transfer or UBO change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted confirmation exposes the manager and the entity to administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 (approx. USD 270,000); criminal penalties can reach EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment for intentionally false statements. After two consecutive unconfirmed years, RBE deletion proceedings may be initiated, threatening the RCS registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and inventory pursuant to Luxembourg commercial accounting law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed for an unregulated SCSp; prepared by the manager and retained at the registered office for inspection by partners, RCS, and the direct-tax administration on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the financial year-end (balance sheet date); approved by the partners unless the partnership agreement prescribes another approval process.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Manager's civil and criminal liability for non-preparation; in insolvency, failure to maintain books may trigger personal liability of the general partner; repeated breaches permit partner-led actions for judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and management certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained at the registered office; available to RCS, RBE, and tax authorities upon official summons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed and signed by the manager during the annual UBO confirmation month, covering the register of partners/managers, minutes, transfer registers, and accounting records custody.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect or unavailable registers expose the manager to criminal sanctions for false records and personal civil liability to creditors; prolonged failure supports administrative strike-off of the RCS registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Public deposit of annual accounts (RCS annual accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the eJustice/MyRBE portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end if the SCSp is subject to public filing (unregulated SCSp generally exempt; filing may be contractually required or chosen by the partners).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If filing is legally or contractually required, late filing triggers a court-ordered filing and fines up to EUR 5,000 per non-compliant year; continued non-compliance after warnings may result in administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT declaration (where the SCSp carries on taxable supplies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return due 31 May following the calendar year if the partnership is admitted to annual VAT filing; monthly/quarterly declarations apply depending on turnover thresholds.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a 10% surcharge plus monthly default interest of 0.6%; after two missed periods, the AEDT may issue an ex-officio assessment and commence tax execution; non-payment does not by itself trigger corporate strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No entity-level audit is compulsory for an unregulated SCSp merely because it is a special limited partnership. Audit is required where (i) the SCSp is a regulated alternative investment fund, (ii) the corporate general partner triggers Luxembourg accounting-law thresholds (at least two of: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, average workforce above 50 employees), or (iii) the partnership agreement expressly requires an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002, as amended (transposing Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for consolidated financial statements; books must be kept in euro for tax-transparent SCSp reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain a beneficial-owner declaration filed with RBE and confirm it annually during the anniversary month of initial registration. Every transfer of a partnership interest, whether general or limited, requires an amended UBO declaration within one month of the transfer. The annual confirmation then verifies that the RBE list of ultimate beneficial owners remains complete and accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers (gérant) and General Partner
